stubs.angle: Asks which of several test descriptions is a unit test rather than an integration or end-to-end test.
stubs.answerHinge: A unit test exercises a small piece of behaviour in isolation from out-of-process dependencies such as databases, file systems and networks, so it is fast and deterministic.

stubs.angle: Asks the candidate to explain the Arrange-Act-Assert structure of a test and why each test should have a single Act step.
stubs.answerHinge: Separating setup, the one action under test and the checks makes a test readable and ensures that a failure points to one behaviour.

stubs.angle: Asks what an xUnit [Theory] with three [InlineData] attributes does compared with a [Fact].
stubs.answerHinge: A [Theory] is a parameterized test that runs once per data row, so three [InlineData] rows give three separately reported test cases, while a [Fact] takes no parameters and runs once.

stubs.angle: Asks the candidate to describe the red-green-refactor cycle of test-driven development and the purpose of each step.
stubs.answerHinge: Write a failing test first to prove it can fail, write the minimal code to make it pass, then refactor with the passing tests as a safety net.

stubs.angle: Asks which signature a test method that awaits an async method under test should have.
stubs.answerHinge: The test must be declared async Task so the test framework can await completion and observe exceptions; an async void test returns nothing the framework can wait on.

stubs.angle: Asks how a mock differs from a fake and when each is the better choice for a dependency.
stubs.answerHinge: A fake is a working lightweight implementation checked through resulting state, while a mock records and verifies interactions, so mocks fit outgoing calls whose occurrence is the behaviour and fakes fit dependencies whose state the test reads back.

stubs.angle: A hand-written console test checks that Parse("") throws by wrapping the call in try/catch (Exception) and printing PASS in the catch. The parser has a bug that throws NullReferenceException, yet the test prints PASS. Find the defective line.
stubs.answerHinge: An exception test must assert the specific expected exception type and fail when no exception or a different one is thrown; catching Exception makes any failure, including a real bug, count as a pass.

stubs.angle: Two hand-written test methods run in sequence against a fake repository that keeps items in a static list, so the second test sees one extra item and prints FAIL; find the line.
stubs.answerHinge: Static state in a test double survives between tests and makes results depend on execution order, so each test needs its own fresh instance.

stubs.angle: Asks which statement correctly describes what WebApplicationFactory<TEntryPoint> does in an ASP.NET Core integration test.
stubs.answerHinge: It starts the application's real entry point on an in-memory TestServer, so requests from its HttpClient pass through the full middleware pipeline without opening a network port, and services can be replaced with ConfigureTestServices.

stubs.angle: Asks which differences make the EF Core in-memory provider an unreliable substitute for a relational database in tests.
stubs.answerHinge: The in-memory provider is not a relational database: it does not enforce relational constraints, has no real transactions, cannot run raw SQL and can accept queries the real provider would fail to translate.

stubs.angle: Asks which statements about using TimeProvider (introduced in .NET 8) to test time-dependent and delay-based code are true.
stubs.answerHinge: Injecting TimeProvider instead of reading DateTime.UtcNow or calling Task.Delay directly lets a test substitute FakeTimeProvider from Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing and advance time explicitly without real waiting.

stubs.angle: About 5 percent of CI runs fail on different tests that always pass locally; what does the candidate do and in what order?
stubs.answerHinge: Retrying hides the defect; the fix is to quarantine the flaky tests and find the nondeterministic source, such as wall-clock time, test order, parallel test collections sharing an external resource, or unawaited async work.

stubs.angle: Asks how to keep integration tests that run against a real database engine in a container isolated from each other and still fast.
stubs.answerHinge: Create the schema once per run and then isolate each test by rolling back a per-test transaction or resetting data to a known state, rather than recreating the database for every test.

stubs.angle: Asks which testing practices make a suite break on refactorings that do not change observable behaviour.
stubs.answerHinge: Tests that verify calls to internal collaborators, verify query calls on stubs or test private methods through reflection couple to implementation details, while asserting on outputs and outgoing side effects survives refactoring.

stubs.angle: After the team introduced an 80 percent line-coverage gate in CI, reviews find tests that call code without meaningful assertions; what does the candidate do as tech lead?
stubs.answerHinge: Coverage shows which code is untested, not that it is tested well, so a hard target invites gaming; treat coverage as a diagnostic, review test quality in code review and consider mutation testing on critical code instead of raising the number.

stubs.angle: Asks how to verify compatibility between many independently deployed services without depending on one shared end-to-end environment.
stubs.answerHinge: Consumer-driven contract tests let each provider check, in its own pipeline, that it still satisfies its consumers' expectations, so only a thin layer of end-to-end tests over critical user journeys remains.
